brief.headline: Push them to ₹290.00/KG on top SKUs (saves ₹32.69 L/yr) and offer 15-day faster payment in exchange for a 2–3% price cut

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290.00/KG on the three biggest items — the price Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd already gives us
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG on top SKUs; total saving ₹32.69 L/yr
priceAsk.basis: We pay Shrinath ₹290.00/KG for the same laminates, but GEEP charges us ₹294.03–₹308.30/KG on those items. The open market for pharma/ORS laminate runs ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so our current price sits at the top of the fair band — there's room to come down to what we already pay elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (drop from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt) in return for a 2–3% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days sooner frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash, but their borrowing rate is 1.55–9.25% (effective 4.38%), so getting cash 15 days earlier is worth about 2% annualised to them — a fair swap for a matching price cut

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only ₹1 of every ₹100 they sell (1.1% profit), so they can't afford a big price squeeze. But their cash is stuck for 81 days while similar firms tie up cash for only 46 days — that means cash is tight for them and they'll value faster payment. We're 9.72% of their total ₹291.36 Cr revenue, so losing us hurts. Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but the agency did it without their help (they stopped sharing info), so treat that number as shaky. Push hard on payment-for-price, not a straight price cut that could tip them over.

evidence.point: We pay ₹32.69 L/yr more than the lowest price we already get
Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd gives us ₹290.00/KG; GEEP charges ₹294.03–₹308.30/KG on the same items
We're a big customer — 9.72% of everything they sell
Their cash is stuck for 81 days, longer than similar firms at 46 days
They keep only 1.1% as profit, so margins are razor-thin
Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our working capital

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying us a little — proven and can scale to cover laminate sachets as a second source

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion; big enough to second-source GEEP at full scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates — a strong second-source fit for GEEP

risks: GEEP is 76% of our laminate spend (₹28.31 Cr) — we're over-concentrated, so qualify and approve a second supplier before you push too hard
Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but the agency said they stopped cooperating — treat their financial health as uncertain and keep supply continuity front of mind
They have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays and pending legal cases — watch for operational hiccups that could disrupt deliveries
Profit is only 1.1% — a big straight price cut could hurt supply; structure the ask as payment-for-price so they get cash relief in return
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're a key partner for us on laminates, but we're paying ₹290/kg to another supplier for the same spec — let's close that gap and talk about how faster payment from our side can help your cash flow.
